text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Silver Cross Insurance managing director Peter Woodcock, whose company tried to launch a special trauma insurance last year, believes the health insurance market is totally uncompetitive as the Department of Health banned his product after the existing health funds went into battle over it. As the Productivity Commission will begin an inquiry into health funds, many with similar experiences believe the funds have been "authors of their own destiny". Page 1.

Under increasing pressure from the Federal Government to pass the Workplace Relations Bill, the Australian Democrats yesterday offered a compromise on the future role of the Industrial Relations Commission. Page 1.

A key Senate report, prepared by Labor and Democrat senators on the Telstra privatisation committee will be released today, with a majority of committee members supporting continued public ownership of the national telecommunications carrier. Page 2.

The New South Wales Health and Research Employees Association said non-nursing employees in the New South Wales health and community services sector will enjoy wage rises of between 18 and 19.2 percent over the next three years, confirming NSW's position as a pace-setter on public sector wages. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Prime Minister John Howard has warned the Labor Opposition that should it go through with its plans to block A$7 billion from the federal gudget, interest rates could rise. Howard's attack signals what strategists believe will be a continued assault on the Opposition as Parliament resumes this week following a two week break after the Budget. Page 1.

The future of the Australian Football League is facing marked changes as the finals series of its centenary season is dominated by interstate teams. With Hawthorn and Geelong swept aside early, only North Melbourne remained as a Melbourne winner after the weekend saw Brisbane, Sydney and Perth's West Coast Eagles snatch victories. Page 1.

Connie Casey, the girlfriend of British tourist Brian Hagland, who was bashed to death on a Bondi street early Saturday morning, has pleaded for help to catch Hagland's killers. The attack was unprovoked and medical centres and hospitals are on alert as it is suspected one of the two male killers was injured during the assault. Page 3.

New South Wales Olympics Minister Michael Knight has said that in his capacity as president of the Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games his first priority would be to unite the 15-member board because of concerns that the committee had not ben performing properly. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The High Court will on Wednesday hear a submission from Australia's Catholic Church whereby it is seeking to be involved as a third party in a case concerning a woman who was unable to have an abortion because her pregnancy was diagnosed too late. Page 1.

Connie Casey will leave Australia with the body of her fiance Brian Hagland after he was murdered by two men outside Jackie's Cafe in Wairoa Avenue Bondi early on Saturday morning. The couple, on a working holiday in Australia, were returning home to their flat when Hagland was beaten and kicked to death in an unprovoked attack. Page 1.

A Herald investigation has found that the people who carried out the rort of the 1994 election of the telecommunications division of the Communication Electrical Plumbing Union are back in business for the September 16 elections, this time distributing thousands of illegal, anonymous, libelous propaganda sheets about their opponents. Page 1.

Public health sources and the water industry have criticised new national guidelines for drinking water quality, saying they fail to set any standards for a range of emerging water-borne disease organisms, such as giardia and cryptosporidium, which are able to resist conventional cleansing treatments and can cause severe diarrhoea and even death in some people with weak immune systems. Page 3.
THE AGE

Figures obtained under the Freedom of Information Act have indicated the number of patients forced to wait on trolleys at St Vincent's and Royal Melbourne hospitals for more than 12 hours have doubled over the past year, with 400 patients left on trolleys at Royal Melbourne this June - a 98 percent increase on last year. Page 1.

The Anti-Discrimination Tribunal has granted an exemption to Belle Voyage, a women-only taxi service that will operate in Melbourne because many females do not trust male drivers. The Tribunal said issues taken into consideration were safety, demand, and the lack of a similar service. Page A1.

The Victorian Education Department is investigating complaints by parents about a poem titled The Lesson, by Roger McGough, which describes a teacher who takes revenge on his students by hacking the students to death and shooting one pupil in the head. The poem was distributed to year nine students at a government secondary school. Page A1.

The Attorney-General's office has refused to rule out the formation of a national register for suspected and convicted paedophiles, after the idea was raised several months ago in a policy paper for an overhaul of family law. The paper includes proposals to establish reciprocal arrangements with other countries on the recognition and enforcement of maintenance orders. Page A3.
